source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
Corn is Cambodia's third most important crop after rice and cassava, and is Cambodia's traditional third major crop historically grown in the country's northeastern-leaning growing areas. Corn used mainly for animal feed accounts for about 75% of total national corn output, while glutinous/waxy corn for direct human consumption makes up most of the remainder. Cambodia has no domestic corn seed-breeding program of its own; farmers rely entirely on seed either imported from neighboring countries or produced domestically by seed companies operating in-country.

National corn production (total harvested, cited to Barrientos 2017c), in thousand tons, with year-on-year growth in parentheses: 2007: 523 (+38.7%); 2008: 612 (+17.0%); 2009: 924 (+51.0%); 2010: 850 (-8.0%); 2011: 717 (-15.7%); 2012: 951 (+32.6%); 2013: 927 (-2.5%); 2014: 624 (-32.7%); 2015: 733 (+17.5%); 2016: 748 (+2.1%). Production has been volatile year to year, tied to weather (drought/flood) shocks and to farmers switching in and out of the crop based on price.

Average corn yield rose from roughly 1-2 tons/ha in the 1960-2000 period, to 3-4 tons/ha by 2007, to about 8 tons/ha in more recent years (cited to Barrientos 2017d) -- attributed mainly to hybrid seed availability and improved farm technique/machinery adoption, not to expanded irrigated area. Nationally cultivated corn area was reported at 163,106 ha in 2008, rising to 215,452 ha in 2013 (cited to Cheng, 2017); dry-season corn area specifically was 142,540 ha in 2016, of which Prey Veng province alone accounted for 21,395 ha.

Note on figures: a separate passage in the source states cultivated corn area grew to about 113,000 ha in 2017, producing about 433,000 tons that year, attributed to the HLH company group (a large private buyer/exporter) reporting roughly 10,000 ha of contracted corn area. This 2017 figure is materially smaller than the 215,452 ha (2013) / 748,000-ton (2016) national figures reported elsewhere in the same document -- the discrepancy likely reflects different scopes (one company's contracted area vs. national totals) rather than an actual production collapse, but both numbers are reported here as they appear in the source without reconciling them.
